precepts.text: Abraham circumcised Isaac at eight days as God commanded, before Moses and with no sacrifice; the Pharisees wanted circumcision with sacrifice because that was their bread and butter, and the more people followed Christ the less they sacrificed.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said”, and “Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.” Sarah conceived in old age and Abraham named the child Isaac. Then: “And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.” “And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.”

Isaac was circumcised on the eighth day, as God commanded, but this was long before Moses. There is no reading of them going and sacrificing animals for it. So even eighth-day circumcision here is not after the manner of Moses. There is circumcision of the fathers, and there is circumcision after the manner of Moses, which carries the sacrifice.

That is how Paul can say in Galatians 5, “if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.” He means circumcised after the manner of Moses, back under the yoke of bondage, taught by the Pharisees that you must be circumcised and sacrifice an animal to be saved. “For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law.” Once the temple was destroyed and the priests scattered, that man had no way to keep it and was finished.

“Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; ye are fallen from grace.” Christ's sacrifice does away with the animal sacrifice, so whoever runs back to animals to atone for sin rejects what Christ did on the cross. Paul is not throwing out the commandments. He is rejecting the sacrifice that was bewitching the Galatians. So “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.”

precepts.text: The mothers gave their sons suck three years; being weaned was a milestone at about that age, not a birthday.
precepts.point: The great feast the day Isaac was weaned was not a birthday celebration. Weaned means finished being breastfed, and the mothers gave their children suck about three years; Abraham was celebrating Isaac coming off his mother's breast at around three years old.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

precepts.why:
The great feast “the same day that Isaac was weaned” was not a birthday celebration. Weaned means finished being breastfed, and the mothers gave their children suck about three years. The mother of the seven brethren says it to her son: “have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee such three years, and nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age.”

Nine months in the womb, three years at the breast. So Abraham was celebrating Isaac coming off his mother’s breast at around three years old; being weaned was the milestone.

precepts.text: The prophecy over Ishmael's posterity: a wild man, his hand against every man, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren.
precepts.point: The word over his lineage stands: a wild people, his hand against every man and every man's hand against him, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren in the Middle East. His mother took him a wife out of Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

precepts.why:
Ishmael “dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.” He learned the skills of combat and war, according to his nature, and that nature was spoken before he was born. The angel of the Lord told Hagar, “thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the Lord hath heard thy affliction. And he will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.”

The word over his lineage stands: a wild people, his hand against every man and every man’s hand against him, dwelling in the presence of all his brethren in the Middle East. He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and “his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.”

points: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian mocking; Ishmael was mocking Isaac. Even to this day the Arabs mock us: they come to America, open corner stores, make money, and look down on black people. Sarah said, Cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac. He gets no inheritance with my son.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: The thing was very grievous in Abraham's sight because of his son; every man loves his kids. So the Most High had to intervene: Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. The righteous seed, the prophets, come through Isaac. And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed: do not worry about your son, he is going to be all right.

points: Abraham rose up early, took bread and a bottle of water, gave it to Hagar, and sent her away with the child. That is important, because the Arabs love to talk about Abraham, we are descendants of Abraham, the Abrahamic religions. Abraham gave you a bottle of water and some bread and sent you away.

points: She wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, the water was spent, she cast the child under a shrub and sat a bow shot away and wept. God heard the voice of the lad, and the angel said, Fear not; arise, lift up the lad, for I will make him a great nation. God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. And God was with the lad, and he grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer. God was with Ishmael. The wilderness is the desert. An archer is a warrior; Ishmael was a warrior. He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, over by Sinai, not far from Egypt, and his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.
